exposure: Pathogen type (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, coagulase-negative Staphylococcus, Streptococcus agalactiae, Staphylococcus aureus, Candida spp)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 297 neonates with culture-proven sepsis in a clinical setting in Guangzhou City.
finding: Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and coagulase-negative Staphylococcus were the top three pathogens causing neonatal sepsis, with specific pathogens linked to early-onset (Streptococcus agalactiae) or late-onset sepsis (K. pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus) and varying clinical characteristics.
